footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$933.8B; net income attributable to shareholders NT$398.3B). Dollar figures are converted at NT$31.05 per US$1 — implied by TSMC's own stated US-dollar revenue of $30.07B. Operating expenses are shown as one line, as in TSMC's earnings release, and segment dollars are the platform figures from TSMC's official consolidated financial statements. The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$29.6B (about $1.0B) — mostly interest earned on TSMC's large cash pile, plus other gains, partly offset by foreign-exchange losses and finance costs.

takeaways.text: Chips made on 7-nanometer and more advanced processes were 74% of wafer revenue — 3nm alone was 24% and 5nm 36% as AI accelerators ramped.
takeaways.title: Leading edge is the business

takeaways.text: A gross margin of 58.6% and an operating margin of 49.6% mean TSMC kept about half of every revenue dollar after running the fabs.
takeaways.title: Margins at very high levels

takeaways.text: Management guided third-quarter revenue to $31.8–33.0B with a gross margin of 55.5–57.5% — a touch below Q2's level, at a stronger assumed NT dollar.
takeaways.title: A stronger Q3 ahead

verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 39% to NT$933.8B ($30.1B) as AI demand kept its most advanced fabs full — and with a 58.6% gross margin, it kept NT$398.3B ($12.8B) as profit, up 61%.
